q: Which annotations does `@SpringBootApplication` combine?
explain: @SpringBootConfiguration is a @Configuration that tests can find. Component scanning starts at the annotated class's package.

q: In Spring Boot 3, how are auto-configuration classes discovered?
explain: Boot 2.7 introduced the imports file, and Boot 3 dropped spring.factories for auto-configuration.

q: You declare your own `DataSource` @Bean. What does Boot's DataSource auto-configuration do?
options: It backs off thanks to @ConditionalOnMissingBean, and yours is used
explain: User configuration is processed before auto-configuration, and most auto-configured beans are conditional on no user bean of that type.

q: How do you find out why an auto-configuration did or didn't apply?
options: Run with --debug (conditions evaluation report) or check /actuator/conditions
Enable TRACE logging for all packages
explain: The report lists positive and negative matches with the exact condition that passed or failed.

q: `spring.datasource.url` is set in application.yml and also as an environment variable. Which wins?
options: Startup fails due to the conflict
explain: Environment variables rank above packaged config files, and only command-line arguments rank above them among the common sources. That's what makes 12-factor style config work.

q: Which environment variable sets `spring.datasource.url`?
explain: Relaxed binding: dots become underscores, upper case, dashes removed. List indexes use `_0_`, as in `MY_LIST_0_NAME`.

q: The main class is in `com.shop.app` and a `@Service` is in `com.shop.billing`. What happens?
options: The service isn't found: scanning starts at com.shop.app
It's found: Boot scans the whole classpath
explain: Put the main class in the root package (`com.shop`), or set `scanBasePackages`.

q: What does `@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)` load?
options: The MVC layer (controllers, advice, converters, filters) but not services or repositories
Only the controller instance, without MVC
explain: Dependencies of the controller must be provided as mocks (@MockitoBean). MockMvc is auto-configured.

q: What does `@DataJpaTest` do by default?
options: Loads JPA components, makes each test transactional and rolls it back, and replaces the DataSource with an embedded one if possible
Loads the full context with a real DB
explain: To test against the real database type, use Testcontainers and `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)` (or @ServiceConnection).

q: Why can many @SpringBootTest classes with different @MockitoBean sets make the test suite slow?
options: Each distinct configuration needs its own application context; the context cache can't reuse them
explain: Spring caches contexts by configuration. Standardize mocks in a shared base class, or prefer slices and plain unit tests.

q: What does `@ServiceConnection` on a Testcontainers container field do?
options: Boot derives connection properties (URL, user, password) from the running container automatically
It starts the container in a separate JVM
It registers the container as a REST client
explain: It replaces manual @DynamicPropertySource code. It's supported for PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, MongoDB and more since Boot 3.1.

q: Which Actuator endpoints map to Kubernetes probes?
explain: Liveness = "restart me if broken". Readiness = "send me traffic". Don't put external dependencies into liveness, or a DB outage restarts every pod.

q: How can you change a logger's level in a running Boot app?
explain: Handy for debugging production temporarily. The endpoint must be exposed and secured.

q: Which embedded server does `spring-boot-starter-web` use by default?
explain: Exclude spring-boot-starter-tomcat and add the Jetty/Undertow starter to switch. WebFlux defaults to Reactor Netty.

q: How do ApplicationRunner and CommandLineRunner differ?
options: ApplicationRunner gets parsed ApplicationArguments; CommandLineRunner gets raw String[] args
CommandLineRunner runs before the context starts
Only one of them can exist per app
explain: Both run after the context is refreshed, just before ApplicationReadyEvent, ordered by @Order.

q: What is a Spring Boot starter?
options: A dependency descriptor that brings a set of libraries (and their auto-configuration) with compatible versions
explain: Starters themselves contain almost no code; the auto-configuration lives in spring-boot-autoconfigure (or a custom -autoconfigure module).

q: What does `server.shutdown=graceful` do?
options: Stops accepting new requests and lets in-flight requests finish within a timeout
Restarts the server instead of stopping
explain: Combined with a Kubernetes preStop delay and readiness turning DOWN, it gives zero-downtime rolling deploys. It's the default since Boot 3.4.

q: In Spring Boot 3, what replaced Spring Cloud Sleuth for distributed tracing?
explain: Micrometer Observation API with Micrometer Tracing bridges (OpenTelemetry or Brave) and exporters such as OTLP or Zipkin.

q: What's the trade-off of `spring.main.lazy-initialization=true`?
options: Faster startup, but misconfiguration errors surface at first use and the first requests are slower
explain: Eager singletons fail fast at startup. Lazy init is handy in development; in production, failing at deploy time is usually better.

q: A `@ConfigurationProperties` record has `@NotNull` fields and the class is `@Validated`. The property is missing. What happens?
options: The application fails to start with a binding validation error
explain: Failing at startup is exactly what you want for missing configuration.

q: Which Actuator endpoints are exposed over HTTP by default in Boot 3?
explain: Since Boot 2.5 only health is exposed over the web by default. Expose more with `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include`, and protect them.

q: How is a Boot fat jar laid out?
options: BOOT-INF/classes, BOOT-INF/lib with nested jars, and Boot's launcher classes
One flattened jar with all classes merged
Only your classes; dependencies are downloaded at startup
explain: Plain Java can't load nested jars, so Boot's JarLauncher sets up a class loader that can. The layered jar index then splits it into Docker layers.

q: In your own starter's auto-configuration, how do you let users replace your default `Client` bean?
options: Document that users must exclude your auto-configuration
explain: User @Configuration is processed first, so a user's `Client` bean makes yours back off.

q: What does `spring-boot-devtools` provide?
options: Automatic restart on classpath changes and LiveReload, disabled in packaged production jars
explain: The restart uses two class loaders (libraries vs your code) to be fast. Devtools turns itself off when the app runs from a fully packaged jar.
